newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA PROVIDES MARKET FOR BITS OTHERS WON'T EAT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA PROVIDES MARKET FOR BITS OTHERS WON'T EAT.

text.p: Foreign poultry and sheep producers had found a ready market in South Africa for products they cannot sell at home, the head of South Africa's farm products marketing council said on Wednesday.

Eckart Kassier, chairman of the National Agricultural Marketing Council, told a parliamentary committee that the exporters could not be accused of dumping because they were not subsidising the products.
"The (local) poultry industry has suffered severely because of the importation of much cheaper meat, mainly from the United States, Canada and France," Kassier said.
"The simple reason is that Americans, Canadians, all they eat is the white meat, the breasts. The wings and drumsticks, they don't eat those.
"We can pick them up in America for next to nothing, and we South Africans seem to prefer that part, so it's coming in very cheaply. If it's not subsidised in any way, then it's not dumping."
Kassier said the same applied to cheap mutton from Australia.
"The Australians don't eat mutton, they eat lamb. We South Africans like mutton, with quite a bit of fat on it. So they found a market here.
"The alternative market for old ewes in Australia was a bullet and they used to bury them. So that's not dumping either," Kassier said.
